executed_calculation.method: Exact conditional Gaussian integration over 2^5=32 frozen Bernoulli shock configurations with conditional Poisson-binomial six-market breadth, plus verified schedule-to-close matrix (7 release clocks x 6 indices = 42 cells). Executed on GitHub Actions Python 3.10 and 3.12. No random sampling, no seed needed; original model seed preserved only as lineage.
executed_calculation.temporal_subtlety: Nominal Dallas Fed Thu 10:30 CT publication is exactly 16:30 UTC, the nominal STOXX600 17:30 CET cash close. Page says 'at or shortly after', so data cannot be guaranteed known before that close. Use conservative strict earlier-than comparison; 2026-11-19 STOXX count one Friday cash close; US has Thu and Fri.
executed_calculation.interpretation: Exact 32-state model expectation 33.10% versus archived 20k MC 32.95% differs by ~0.15 percentage points due to finite Monte Carlo and CDF approximation. Shared-shock coupling adds ~1.70 points versus a shadow benchmark with the same marginal tail probabilities. Calendar-varying synthetic shocks show event-time exposure can change model-calculated breadth risk substantially. Synthetic shocks are not estimated event responses and cannot be scored as forecasts.

status_and_limitations: Sunday official macro releases for Nov16–20 have not occurred; did not insert future realized data or newly freeze a weekly forecast.

Existing 5 generic shocks are not tied to release timestamps, so the temporal gate tests a proposed model design and not historical forecast skill.
Normal innovations and event probabilities uncalibrated; interval and Brier comparison requires 26 or more prospective weekly paired cohorts.
Market calendars assume ordinary weekday sessions; actual exchanges, early closes and delayed publication must be audited before automatic live use.
WTI matched NYMEX contract still unresolved; this study intentionally excludes WTI and uses six equity indices only.
